messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood demo — post-call recap + proposed prioritized bake-off plan

Susan / team — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a proposed, prioritized set of tests so we can make the hyperscaler comparison actionable for your eval committee. I kept this tight to make sign-offs straightforward.

Key context from call:
- Goal: decide between running inference on hyperscaler-managed endpoints vs Redwood Dedicated (predictable latency + routing) within 6 weeks.
- Primary constraints: P95 latency under 220ms for short-chat loads, cost target <$0.003/token for 512-token bursts, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Proposed prioritized test list (short -> long):
1) Latency & stability (short prompts, 128/512 tokens): P50/P95/P99 across regions (us-west/us-east). Owner: Ben.
2) Throughput at scale (continuous 16-concurrent streams, 1K tokens/session): measure sustained tokens/sec and GPU utilization. Owner: Rishi.
3) Cold-start and scaling behavior (scale from 0 -> target concurrency): track tail latency and warm-up time. Owner: Priyom.
4) Cost-per-token baseline (same model family quantized on both platforms): measure per-token billing and actual token compute cost. Owner: Ben.
5) Functional parity & hallucination regression (50 canonical prompts + 20 negative tests): quality check and output diffs. Owner: Rishi.

Deliverables and timelines:
- Test harness + scripts committed to a shared Drive folder by Wed 11/11 (Ben + Rishi).
- Run initial latency & throughput passes 11/12–11/14.
- Scorecard (P50/P95/cost/quality) and recommendation 11/15 morning.

Attachments: neptune-bakeoff-plan-v1.xlsx (test matrix + sample prompts), redwood-test-matrix.md (execution notes).

Next asks for you: please confirm (A) the priority order above, (B) any must-have scenarios we missed, and (C) whether procurement needs an NDA or SOC2 doc before we start tests. If you prefer, we can lock a 30-min runbook review on Tue 11/10.

Thanks — I’ll pause on running anything until we have your go-ahead.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine — super helpful, thanks. Quick answers from our side:
- Priority order looks good. Please bump "Cold-start" to priority 2 if possible; our product has bursty traffic and tail behavior is a key decision factor.
- Must-have scenario: multi-tenant isolation check (same model, different customer inputs) — we need to ensure no cross-request KV leakage. Add as a short hygiene test.
- Procurement: we can share a redacted SOC2 report internally but will need a technical contact for any follow-ups. No NDA required for the initial run.

Also: Tim from CloudEdge is looping in to confirm they can replicate our baseline tests on their managed endpoints — would be great to have aligned metrics.

If you can move Cold-start up and add the multi-tenant isolation check (small test), we can greenlight the latency/scale runs this Friday (11/12).

Thanks — I can take latency/stability and cost-per-token. Quick technical notes and proposed test harness approach so we all run the same thing:

Recommended harness: k6 + a small Python runner that hits both Redwood and hyperscaler endpoints using identical prompt streams. Benefits: reproducible, lightweight results, and standard CSV outputs we can ingest into the scorecard.

Test matrix (high level):
- Latency/stability: 128 / 512 / 2048 token lengths; 1, 8, 16 concurrent streams; 30-min steady-state windows. Metrics: P50/P95/P99, error rate, restart count.
- Cold-start: from zero to 16 streams. Measure time-to-stable-P95 and percent of requests > 500ms during ramp.
- Isolation: run parallel sessions with correlated inputs and inspect KV headers/logs for leakage (where logs are accessible). If logs aren’t accessible on hyperscaler endpoints, we'll use blackbox output diffing plus synthetic markers.
- Throughput/cost: use a quantized variant where available and measure token/sec/GPU and dollars/token from billing feeds. We'll normalize for model family and quantization level in the scorecard.
- Quality: run 50 canonical prompts + 20 adversarial prompts. Use automated string-similarity + human spot checks for hallucination counts.

Owners and timeline (adjusted per Susan):
- Latency/stability + cost: Ben — run 11/12–11/13; deliver raw CSVs by EOD 11/13.
- Cold-start + isolation: Priyom — run 11/12 (scaled ramp) and 11/13 (isolation); deliver notes by 11/14 AM.
- Quality suite + diff: Rishi — run by 11/14, human spot-check completed 11/15 AM.

I’ll drop the initial k6 scripts and a README into the Drive folder this afternoon. Susan — do you have a preferred place to push results (your S3 or should we share Drive links)? Also tagging procurement: Ben can be technical contact for SOC2 follow-ups if needed.
